body.opens: A source can be relied on and read purely only if one can know whether its content changed, by a hash, a version or an ETag; keeping its past is the integration's choice, an FTP reader caching what it reads becoming a store of its own.

A reference into any source, read where a type is asked, resolves in place to a value of that type, at a point, a head or now: a search bar's buffer read as a string, a git blob as text, a channel as a signal. Whether it is first class, and whether the type, the source or both resolve, is open; the session's lean, both, a mismatch refused.

Two independent questions: whether the engine runs a thing and governs its running, and whether it serves the engine as a source or consumes it as the interface does. 13/19's a store is never a program mixed the two.

name: Who runs it, and what it speaks

body.opens: What the interface needs of the engine, to read, be told and commit, everything else meeting it needs too; the interface a primitive for drawing through components, not for how it connects; whether integrations and the interface are programs, the author's to hold.
FTP, git, HTTP and the file system all give directories and files, a type many sources may show, so one component may show any of them.

name: Directories and files as a shared type

body.opens: The heads a change was made from, settled at 12/57 and not built, recorded in the commit: stopping a silent overwrite of a shared list, giving a commit causal parents for peers, and letting writers see what each had heard. The free agents', not yet weighed by the author.

body.kept: Whole in the author's words: every utterance as it came, typed the first and the last, spoken between, the dictation's stray 333333 kept as written. The session's answers by their essence, short; the four free agents' reports are kept only as woven into answer 10.

name: A sixteenth session: the source both ways again, the buffer gathered, and resolution where sources meet types
